## Macro Backdrop

US equity markets staged a partial tech recovery overnight after the Nasdaq suffered its worst single-day decline in 19 months last Thursday (–5.52%). A rebound in Asian equities, led by Japan (+3.1–3.5%), is setting up a constructive open. The key near-term catalyst is **October CPI**, due tomorrow (Nov 10) — the Cleveland Fed's nowcast puts it at 3.88% YoY, still above the Fed's 2% target. The 10-year Treasury yield sits near 4.87–4.88%, off its recent highs, while Brent crude has pulled back to ~$97/bbl on easing Iran escalation fears after Trump called further strikes "highly unlikely." Gold remains elevated at ~$4,120/oz. The Fed's December meeting remains in focus; a stronger-than-expected jobs print last week revived rate-hike speculation. Q3 S&P 500 earnings season is winding down — 84% of reporters beat, but the average beat margin is a thin 2.7%, the weakest in four years.

## POET Technologies (POET) Daily Update

**Current Price:** ~$4.41–$5.10 intraday range (Nov 8); closed ~$5.07 on Nov 6 (+19.0% that session). 52-week range: $3.87–$20.81. Year-to-date: approximately –20%.

**News in Last 24 Hours:** No new press releases or SEC filings detected for November 8–9. Next major catalyst is **Q3 2026 earnings on November 16**. New CFO Giovanni Pacelli (replacing Thomas Mika) has been in seat since November 2.

---

### Key Risk Status

| Risk | Status |
|---|---|
| **(1) Marvell/Celestial AI order cancellation & NDA** | Marvell notified POET on April 23, 2026 that it was canceling all Celestial AI purchase orders, citing POET's alleged breach of confidentiality obligations (CFO Mika's public comments about the relationship). Stock dropped ~47% on disclosure (April 27). No confirmed contract lawsuit by Marvell against POET as of this writing; the NDA breach is the stated basis for cancellation. POET has identified a ~$5M replacement order from another technology company. |
| **(2) Securities class actions (PFIC misrepresentation)** | Multiple law firms (Rosen, Faruqi & Faruqi, Kirby McInerney, DJS Law, SueWallSt) filed federal securities class actions; class period April 1–27, 2026; District of New Jersey. Allegations: POET failed to disclose its likely PFIC (passive foreign investment company) tax status, which could impose punitive US tax treatment on shareholders. POET disclosed in a Form 6-K that it was classified as a PFIC for 2025 and may be in future years; the company intends to redomicile in the US. Lead plaintiff deadline passed June 29, 2026 — cases now proceeding. |
| **(3) Capital raise / dilution impact** | January 2026: POET priced a **$150M registered direct offering** (note: not $400M as sometimes cited). With continuing operating losses and a business model that burns cash, further dilution remains a risk. Analysts have flagged this alongside potential upside from the Lumilens relationship (potential $500M+). |

---

### Outlook: **Neutral-to-Cautious** (short-term) / **Speculative** (medium-term)

The stock has stabilized above its cash value after the April disaster, and the November 16 earnings call is the next real data point. Until POET shows a credible replacement revenue path post-Marvell, the litigation overhang and dilution risk keep the stock range-bound. Any positive news on Lumilens or a new hyperscaler relationship could be a significant re-rating catalyst.
